jobs.title: People Systems Specialist
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is hiring an HRIS Systems Administrator to serve as the go-to resource for Workday and help build a scalable, reliable, and efficient HR technology foundation. This role will support the implementation and go-live of Workday HCM while owning ongoing system configuration, reporting, maintenance, troubleshooting, automation, and continuous optimization. You will partner closely with People & Culture, Payroll, Finance, IT, Business Systems, implementation partners, and business stakeholders to ensure Workday delivers accurate data, efficient processes, and an intuitive experience for employees and managers.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Support the implementation, testing, data validation, cutover, go-live, and post-launch stabilization of Workday HCM in partnership with internal stakeholders and implementation partners

  • Serve as the primary Workday resource post-go-live for People & Culture and business users, providing day-to-day functional support, troubleshooting issues, and coordinating escalations as needed

  • Configure and maintain Workday HCM business processes, organizational structures, job profiles, positions, notifications, eligibility rules, security roles, and related system functionality

  • Develop and maintain Workday reports, dashboards, calculated fields, and data extracts that support operational, compliance, and leadership needs

  • Manage ongoing system maintenance, including release testing, regression testing, configuration documentation, data audits, access reviews, and change-control activities

  • Partner cross-functionally to gather requirements, recommend scalable system solutions, improve data quality, streamline manual processes, and strengthen the employee and manager experience

  • Identify and implement opportunities to automate workflows, eliminate manual and redundant processes, and optimize Workday functionality to improve efficiency, scalability, data integrity, and the employee and manager experience.

  • Proactively assess existing HR processes and system usage to identify opportunities for simplification, automation, and continuous improvement, partnering with stakeholders to translate business needs into scalable technology solutions.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 2–5 years of experience in HRIS administration, HR technology, or a related systems role

  • Hands-on experience administering and supporting Workday HCM, including business process configuration, organizational structures, reporting, and system maintenance

  • Experience supporting a Workday implementation, deployment, optimization, or major system go-live, including testing and data validation

  • Experience developing Workday custom reports, dashboards, and calculated fields

  • Strong understanding of core HR processes, employee data, organizational structures, and the employee lifecycle

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to translate business requirements into practical system solutions

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain a high level of accuracy, and handle sensitive employee information with discretion

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

WHOOP is hiring a Senior Electrical Engineer to play a key role in the design and development of next-generation charging platforms and supporting hardware for WHOOP wearable technology. As a member of the Hardware Engineering team, you will own critical electrical designs and subsystems, translating product and system requirements into robust, highly integrated hardware. You will work closely with Electrical, Mechanical, Firmware, Systems, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Product teams to make design tradeoffs, develop and validate new hardware, and bring complex electrical systems from early development through high-volume production.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own electrical designs and subsystems, translating system requirements into electrical specifications, component selections, schematics, and production-ready hardware

  • Design highly integrated, miniaturized, low-power, mixed-signal electronics, making thoughtful tradeoffs across performance, power, size, cost, reliability, manufacturability, and schedule

  • Drive electrical designs from concept through schematic capture, PCB layout and design review, prototype bring-up, characterization, debugging, design iteration, verification, and production

  • Partner closely with Electrical, Mechanical, Firmware, Systems, Manufacturing, and other engineering teams to define interfaces, contribute to system-level tradeoffs, and ensure electrical designs perform reliably within the complete product

  • Evaluate new components, technologies, and design approaches that enable future product capabilities and improve electrical system performance

  • Support NPI and high-volume manufacturing by partnering with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, suppliers, and contract manufacturers on design for manufacturability, functional testing, failure analysis, and production ramp

  • Strong electrical engineering fundamentals across analog and digital circuit design, power architecture and power management, component selection, communication interfaces, and debugging of complex electrical systems

jobs.title: Assistant General Counsel, Litigation
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

The WHOOP legal team plays a critical role in supporting that mission by enabling the business to move quickly and responsibly around the world. We are rigorous but pragmatic, risk-aware rather than risk-averse, calm under pressure, excellent communicators, and deeply committed to being trusted partners to the business.

WHOOP is hiring an Assistant General Counsel, Litigation to oversee and manage litigation and regulatory enforcement matters. In this role, you will report to the Chief Legal Officer (CLO) and, in conjunction with the CLO, be responsible for developing and implementing litigation and regulatory enforcement strategy. The successful candidate must be comfortable managing all manner of litigation, including commercial disputes, consumer class actions, intellectual property matters, employment disputes, and investigations by federal, state, and international regulatory bodies.

WHOOP is a rapidly scaling, global business built upon a dynamic consumer brand that involves hardware, software, and healthcare. Accordingly, this role will be engaged with an extraordinarily broad array of legal areas. The successful candidate will be a seasoned litigator who possesses the first-hand experience and judgment necessary to assess litigation and regulatory risks and opportunities, hire and manage the outside counsel representing WHOOP, and ensure WHOOP receives the highest quality representation from its law firm partners.

In addition to managing the litigation docket, you will serve as a strategic counselor to all business and corporate functions regarding legal risk and opportunity. The successful candidate will be more than an experienced litigator. They will be a business-minded litigation leader who knows when to fight, when to settle, and when litigation risk should drive changes in the business.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the Company's litigation portfolio, with responsibility for the strategy, oversight, and resolution of lawsuits, arbitrations, pre-litigation disputes, and other contested matters involving the Company, independently driving matters while exercising sound judgment as to when legal, business, or reputational risks warrant escalation.

  • Develop litigation strategy for significant matters, including evaluating claims and defenses, determining strategic objectives, identifying key decision points, and recommending litigation and settlement positions.

  • Provide senior leadership with clear and actionable assessments of litigation risk, including exposure, ranges of potential outcomes, strategic alternatives, costs, business implications, and recommended courses of action.

  • Select, retain, and manage outside counsel, establishing clear expectations regarding strategy, staffing, budgets, work product, responsiveness, and outcomes, and independently pressure-testing outside counsel’s strategic recommendations throughout the entire litigation life-cycle.

  • Exercise rigorous oversight of litigation spending, including reviewing budgets and forecasts, scrutinizing staffing and billing practices, identifying opportunities for alternative fee arrangements, and ensuring that legal spending is proportionate to the Company's exposure and strategic objectives.

  • Develop settlement strategies and lead significant settlement negotiations, balancing legal exposure, litigation costs, business considerations, precedent risk, reputational considerations, and operational impacts.

  • Partner closely with Finance and Accounting regarding litigation reserves, contingent liabilities, insurance recoveries, settlement accounting, budgeting and forecasting, and other financial implications of litigation.

  • Partner closely with the People Team regarding employment disputes.

  • Manage litigation-related insurance matters, including providing timely notice of claims, coordinating with insurers and brokers, pursuing available coverage, and managing coverage disputes where necessary.

  • Oversee discovery and evidence-preservation obligations, including litigation holds, document collection and review, information governance, e-discovery strategy, privilege issues, and the use of technology and outside vendors to manage discovery efficiently.

  • Conduct and oversee sensitive internal investigations where appropriate and coordinate with employment, compliance, privacy, security, or other specialists depending on the subject matter.

  • Establish and continuously improve litigation playbooks, processes, and technology, enabling the Legal team to manage a growing litigation portfolio efficiently and consistently as the Company scales.

  • Promote appropriate use of data and technology in litigation management, including e-discovery tools, matter-management systems, litigation analytics, and emerging AI-enabled legal technologies.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • J.D. from an accredited law school and active membership in at least one U.S. state bar.

  • 7+ years of relevant legal experience, including experience at a nationally recognized law firm and/or an in-house legal department managing litigation.

  • Experience as the lead or managing attorney on complex litigation. Strong command of litigation strategy and procedure, including discovery, dispositive motions, expert practice, mediation, trial preparation, settlement negotiations, and appeals.

  • Demonstrated ability to balance legal risk with practical business considerations and deliver actionable advice in a fast-paced environment.

  • Ability to translate complicated legal issues into concise, practical advice for senior executives and business leaders.

  • Experience in building and improving legal processes, playbooks, and operational infrastructure to support a scaling business.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across cross-functional teams.

  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

  • Experience supporting technology, consumer products, healthcare, or subscription-based businesses is strongly preferred.

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

*This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify to determine employment eligibility

The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.

At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $220,000 to $250,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.

In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

These ranges may be modified in the future to reflect evolving market conditions and organizational needs. While most offers will typically fall toward the starting point of the range, total compensation will depend on the candidate’s specific qualifications, expertise, and alignment with the role’s requirements.

jobs.title: Component Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is hiring a Component Engineer to help ensure the electronic components that power our products meet the highest standards for performance, reliability, quality, cost, and supply continuity. In this role, you will own critical aspects of component selection, qualification, lifecycle management, and risk mitigation while partnering closely with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, quality, and external suppliers. You will support both new product development and sustaining programs, helping WHOOP make informed component decisions and build scalable processes that strengthen our hardware development and manufacturing ecosystem.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Research, evaluate, select, and qualify electronic components for new product development and sustaining programs, ensuring alignment with design, performance, reliability, regulatory, and cost requirements.

  • Own component lifecycle and supply risk management, including technical triage of Product Change Notifications, obsolescence planning, alternate component qualification, single-source risk mitigation, and supply continuity initiatives.

  • Maintain and improve component libraries, specifications, lifecycle data, and BOM health information in partnership with Procurement and cross-functional teams, ensuring accurate visibility into component status, sourcing risk, alternate availability, and other key attributes.

  • Partner with electrical engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and procurement teams to resolve component-related technical issues, support failure analysis and root cause investigations, and identify opportunities for cost, quality, and reliability improvements.

  • Collaborate directly with component manufacturers, distributors, and external partners to evaluate technologies, resolve technical issues, develop alternate sources, and support component qualification and sourcing strategies.

  • Develop and continuously improve processes for component selection, qualification, standardization, lifecycle management, compliance, and data quality across both NPI and sustaining programs.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 5+ years of experience in electronic component engineering, component management, electrical engineering, or a related hardware engineering role.

  • Strong knowledge of electronic components such as semiconductors, resistors, capacitors, connectors, and other electrical components, including their applications, manufacturing considerations, and use in electronic designs.

  • Experience with component selection, qualification, lifecycle management, electrical testing, reliability requirements, failure analysis, and alternate component evaluation.

  • Familiarity with component lifecycle and BOM management practices, including obsolescence, Product Change Notifications, sourcing risk, alternate availability, and component management or PLM systems.

  • Working knowledge of relevant industry and regulatory requirements such as RoHS, UL, IPC, and other standards applicable to electronic hardware products.

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to identify technical or supply risks and drive cross-functional actions through resolution in a fast-paced hardware environment.

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

jobs.title: Staff Hardware Engineering Program Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is seeking a Staff Hardware Engineering Program Manager to lead the development of new products. This is a player-coach type role, involving both direct management and project management responsibilities. In this role, you will partner closely with Hardware, Software, Manufacturing, and Creative teams to deliver novel WHOOP hardware. You will be a vital part of the growing Hardware EPM team.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead and align multi-disciplinary engineering teams, including Electrical, Mechanical, Firmware, Sensors and Manufacturing, to deliver new WHOOP hardware products.

  • Manage the engineering project management team dedicated to your program domain, ensuring everyone on your team is working towards the same goals.

  • Build and maintain visibility to the sub-projects within your domain, advising executive leadership on prioritization and team allocation based on business needs.

  • Coordinate critical milestones with cross-functional partners, such as Product, Industrial Design, and UX.

  • Drive clarity and alignment cross-functionally, even when requirements are ambiguous or in-flux.

  • Manage complex integrated projects from kickoff through launch, keeping in mind performance, schedule, and cost goals.

  • Create and manage detailed project schedules based on the product goals, balancing timelines, resources, and risks.

  • Work with the engineering managers to lead the project team through strategic and tactical shifts, keeping everyone focused on the most critical elements of the project.

  • Drive the development builds from Prototype through DVT with internal and external vendor partners.

  • Drive prioritization and planning of test activities with the Technical Leads, from focused design-of-experiments (DOEs) to large-scale beta tests.

  • Communicate project updates and drive key decisions at the executive level.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or equivalent practical experience in hardware product development

  • 8+ years of industry experience in consumer electronics

  • Previous management experience is preferred, but not required.

  • Demonstrated success managing cross-functional hardware projects from development through market release with multiple products launched to date.

  • Strong understanding of product component development cycles, lead times, and sourcing processes

  • Experience communicating with Hardware, Firmware, Manufacturing, and external partners both domestically and internationally

  • Working knowledge of hardware lead-times and electrical development workflows.

  • Strong organizational, multi-tasking, and time management skills with the ability to thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, both written and verbal.

  • Ability to travel internationally to support engineering builds (up to 10%).

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

jobs.title: Global Supply Manager (Electrical Components)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is hiring a Global Supply Manager (EE) to lead sourcing strategy and supplier management for critical electrical components and assemblies across new product introduction (NPI) and sustaining programs. In this role, you will operate at the intersection of Hardware Engineering, Operations, and the global supply base to ensure technology, cost, quality, capacity, and supply continuity support product innovation and successful launches. You will combine technical expertise, commercial judgment, and data-driven decision making to build a resilient and scalable electrical supply chain that supports the long-term growth of WHOOP.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own global sourcing and commodity strategies for electrical components and assemblies, including semiconductors, sensors, batteries, PCBAs, displays, connectors, and other critical technologies, establishing supplier, cost, capacity, and risk roadmaps across NPI and sustaining products.

  • Partner closely with Electrical Engineering and cross-functional teams throughout the product development lifecycle to influence technology and supplier selection, component architecture, design-for-supply-chain decisions, and supplier readiness for development builds, product ramps, and mass production.

  • Lead supplier identification, evaluation, qualification, selection, and ongoing management, balancing technical capability, cost, quality, capacity, geographic footprint, technology roadmaps, and supply continuity while driving supplier performance through structured business reviews and corrective actions.

  • Lead commercial negotiations and cost strategy across assigned commodities, including pricing, cost models, competitive benchmarking, development agreements, capacity commitments, and long-term supply arrangements, identifying opportunities to improve cost without compromising quality, performance, reliability, or member experience.

  • Proactively identify and mitigate supply, capacity, technology, geopolitical, and single-source risks through alternate-source qualification, capacity planning, strategic inventory, supplier investments, and other business continuity strategies.

  • Develop a deep understanding of electrical component markets, supplier capabilities, technology roadmaps, cost structures, lead times, and capacity trends, translating market intelligence and data into actionable recommendations and measurable business outcomes in partnership with Engineering, Materials, Quality, Operations, Finance, and manufacturing partners.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 3+ years of experience in global supply management, strategic sourcing, commodity management, supplier management, or a related function within a hardware or electronics environment, with experience supporting NPI and high-volume production.

  • Experience sourcing electrical components or assemblies, with an understanding of markets and cost structures across technologies such as semiconductors, sensors, batteries, PCBAs, displays, or connectors; consumer electronics experience is a plus.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute commodity or category strategies spanning supplier selection, cost roadmaps, capacity planning, supplier performance, and supply risk mitigation.

  • Strong commercial, analytical, negotiation, and structured problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex cost structures, supplier capabilities, capacity constraints, and supply chain tradeoffs while balancing technical and business objectives.

  • Experience working with global suppliers and manufacturing partners and the ability to influence technical and business decisions through data, subject matter expertise, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Willingness to travel domestically and internationally, approximately 15%, to support supplier engagement, manufacturing readiness, negotiations, and business reviews.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to take ownership, navigate ambiguity, and move effectively between long-term strategy and immediate execution priorities.

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.

At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $120,000.00 - $160,000.00 Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Lead - Growth
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we’re on a mission to unlock human performance. WHOOP empowers its members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is looking for a Lifecycle Marketing Lead – Growth to own lifecycle strategies across Apparel & Accessories, Refer a Friend, and the promotional calendar. This role is ideal for a highly analytical marketer who can move seamlessly between strategy and execution. You’ll dig into performance and member data to identify opportunities, form hypotheses, and translate insights into action. With an experimentation-first mindset, you’ll test and learn quickly, continually finding new ways to engage members and drive measurable business impact.

The ideal candidate is a member-centric, data-driven marketer who can move seamlessly between strategy and execution. You know how to turn insights into action, test and learn quickly, and continually find new ways to engage members and drive measurable business impact.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own the lifecycle strategy and performance for Apparel & Accessories, driving product discovery, cross-sell, repeat purchase, and incremental bookings.

  • Own the Refer a Friend lifecycle strategy, identifying and testing opportunities to increase awareness, participation, and referral activity.

  • Lead the lifecycle promotional calendar, defining how promotional moments come to life across owned channels while balancing growth goals with the member experience.

  • Translate member behavior, performance data, and business insights into strategies, experiments, and growth opportunities.

  • Own the test-and-learn cycle from hypothesis through measurement, interpreting experiment results and using learnings to determine what to scale, iterate, or stop.

  • Develop coordinated experiences across email, SMS, in-app, and other owned channels throughout the member journey.

  • Partner cross-functionally across the Growth, Marketing, Creative, Analytics, and Commercial teams to bring high-impact lifecycle initiatives to life.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of experience in lifecycle, CRM, retention, or growth marketing, with a track record of driving measurable business impact.

  • Experience developing multi-channel lifecycle strategies across email, SMS, and in-app.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to turn data and member insights into clear strategies, experiments, and decisions.

  • Experience with segmentation, personalization, experimentation, and CRM program development.

  • A member-centric, growth-oriented mindset—curious, creative, entrepreneurial, and constantly looking for opportunities to improve performance.

  • Technical fluency with CRM and marketing technology and lifecycle measurement. Experience with Iterable, Amplitude, or Hightouch is a plus.

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and project management skills, with the ability to independently own multiple programs from strategy through execution.

  • Experience in a subscription, e-commerce, or consumer technology business is a plus.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

jobs.title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer (NPI)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock human performance. WHOOP empowers users to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

As a Senior Manufacturing Engineer, you will be responsible for developing manufacturing solutions that enable new products from early design through production ramp. You will work closely with Product Design, Mechanical, Electrical, Quality, and factory engineering teams to influence product design, define assembly strategies, and develop the fixtures, tooling, equipment, and processes required to manufacture products at scale.

You will apply strong mechanical design fundamentals, DFX expertise, and hands-on manufacturing experience to identify manufacturing risks early, translate product requirements into robust manufacturing solutions, and solve complex technical challenges with a high degree of independence.

Responsibilities:

  • Partner closely with Product Design and Mechanical Engineering throughout product development to drive DFM, DFA, and DFX, identifying manufacturing risks and influencing product designs for assembly, quality, scalability, automation, and cost.

  • Develop manufacturing concepts and assembly strategies from early prototypes through production, translating product requirements into practical manufacturing processes, tooling, and equipment.

  • Design and develop fixtures, tooling, nests, gauges, and manufacturing aids used for assembly, alignment, bonding, welding, inspection, and test.

  • Own fixture and tooling development from concept through detailed design, tolerance analysis, fabrication, debugging, qualification, and release to production.

  • Apply GD&T, tolerance analysis, datum strategies, and mechanical design principles to ensure product and fixture designs support repeatable manufacturing and measurement.

  • Work with product engineering teams to evaluate component interfaces, assembly sequences, joining methods, tolerance stack-ups, and other design characteristics that impact manufacturability.

  • Develop and qualify manufacturing processes including adhesive bonding, heat staking, mechanical assembly, and other processes used in small consumer electronic devices.

  • Define critical process parameters, process windows, acceptance criteria, and controls to ensure manufacturing processes consistently meet product requirements.

  • Evaluate manual and automated assembly approaches and develop fixture and equipment concepts that enable appropriate levels of automation.

  • Use DOEs, process characterization, capability analysis, and failure analysis to validate manufacturing designs and optimize process performance.

  • Troubleshoot complex product, fixture, and process interactions during development builds and production ramp, driving issues to root cause and implementing robust engineering solutions.

  • Collaborate directly with contract manufacturers, equipment vendors, and tooling suppliers to develop, review, debug, and qualify manufacturing solutions.

  • Provide hands-on technical support during prototype builds, engineering validation, process qualification, and production ramp.

  • Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support development builds, tooling and equipment qualification, and production ramp.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field.

  • 5+ years of manufacturing engineering experience supporting product development and moderate- to high-volume manufacturing.

  • Ability to operate independently in fast-paced product development and manufacturing environments with limited technical oversight.

  • Strong experience applying DFM, DFA, and DFX principles during product development, with demonstrated ability to influence product designs for manufacturing.

  • Strong proficiency in SolidWorks, including detailed mechanical design, assemblies, drawings, and fixture design best practices.

  • Strong knowledge of GD&T, datum structures, tolerance analysis, tolerance stack-ups, and dimensional inspection methods.

  • Experience developing and qualifying manufacturing processes for small electromechanical or battery-powered electronic products.

  • Experience with manufacturing technologies including adhesives, heat staking, injection-molded plastics, and automated and manual assembly.

  • Strong understanding of injection-molded plastic part design principles, tooling considerations, defect modes, and their interaction with downstream assembly processes.

  • Experience designing and executing DOEs, process characterization studies, capability analyses, and structured failure investigations.

  • Strong hands-on mechanical/electrical and analytical problem-solving skills with the ability to independently develop solutions to complex product and manufacturing challenges.

  • Experience working directly with contract manufacturers, equipment vendors, tooling suppliers, and cross-functional product development teams.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

jobs.title: Senior Analyst, Commercial Analytics (Digital Commerce)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life.

WHOOP is hiring a Senior Analyst to join the Commercial Analytics team and serve as a key analytics partner to our Digital Commerce business. In this role, you will own analysis and reporting across our direct-to-consumer and marketplace channels, translating data into insights that inform pricing, promotions, merchandising, and product strategy. You will help us understand what drives bookings, conversion, and margin across our digital storefronts and partner closely with Marketing Analytics to connect acquisition and traffic trends to downstream commercial performance.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Serve as a key analytics partner to the Digital Commerce team, analyzing performance across direct-to-consumer and marketplace channels to identify opportunities that drive bookings, conversion, and margin growth.

  • Own analysis of digital pricing and promotions, including incrementality, cannibalization, discount depth, and pull-forward, to inform promotional strategy and investment decisions.

  • Analyze funnel and conversion performance, merchandising, product mix, attach rate, and average order value to understand the drivers of digital commerce performance and identify opportunities for growth.

  • Own marketplace performance analysis, evaluating channel economics, assortment, pricing, and customer behavior across marketplaces and our direct-to-consumer business.

  • Build scalable reporting and analytical tools that give Digital Commerce leadership visibility into channel performance, partnering with Analytics Engineering to ensure data is accurate, consistent, and trusted.

  • Support commercial planning and forecasting by developing Digital Commerce inputs and channel-level drivers, and partner with Marketing Analytics to connect acquisition and traffic trends to downstream commercial outcomes.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 4+ years of experience in analytics, business intelligence, or a related discipline, ideally within e-commerce, direct-to-consumer, marketplace, subscription, or consumer products businesses.

  • Strong SQL skills and experience working with large-scale transactional and behavioral data, with the ability to independently move from a business question to analysis, insight, and recommendation.

  • Demonstrated experience building reporting and analytical tools that enable stakeholders to understand performance and make informed business decisions.

  • Strong business acumen and experience partnering with e-commerce, commercial, merchandising, or other business stakeholders, with the ability to synthesize complex data into clear recommendations and actions.

  • Experience with digital commerce analytics, including funnel and conversion analysis, pricing and promotional measurement, merchandising, product mix, or marketplace performance.

  • Familiarity with experimentation and incrementality measurement, digital analytics or clickstream data, and business intelligence tools such as Sigma is a plus.

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Design Research
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we’re on a mission to unlock human performance and healthspan. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies, behaviors, and daily lives.

WHOOP is hiring an Associate Director of Design Research to lead and scale the Design Research practice at WHOOP. This role will oversee Design Research, shaping how user feedback and experiences inform product innovation from early-stage insights to pre-launch validation studies to post-launch feedback. As a people-first leader, you will balance strategic direction, team development, and leadership evangalism—ensuring research rigor, creativity, and impact across the product lifecycle.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Provide strategic leadership for the design research team, ensuring alignment with key stakeholders and organizational priorities.

  • Evangelize the importance of user insights and the role of design research in the product and hardware development lifecycle to WHOOP senior leadership.

  • Scale research impact, working closely with cross-functional leaders to identify opportunities for research and set expectations for mixed-methods research, ensuring research is positioned as a critical input to decision-making.

  • Partner closely with senior team members to review research needs, assess tradeoffs, and guide prioritization and research direction.

  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of design researchers, fostering strong research craft, clear communication, and professional growth.

  • Own relationships with external research vendors, including scoping projects, defining success criteria, and ensuring high-quality execution.

  • Build a strong, cross-functional “voice of the member” for product decision-making in partnership with Consumer Insights, Analytics, and Membership Services.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field such as human factors, design research, user experience research, design anthropology, psychology, or a related discipline.

  • 5+ years of experience conducting user research for physical products, ideally within hardware, health, or consumer product environments.

  • 5+ years of people management experience, including coaching, feedback, and performance development.

  • Strong mixed-methods research background, with demonstrated application of qualitative and quantitative approaches to real-world products.

  • Experience working within or alongside hardware development lifecycles (not software-only).

  • Experience managing or partnering with external research vendors, including project scoping and execution.

  • Ability to manage multiple workstreams, navigate ambiguity, and influence without direct authority across cross-functional teams.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex insights to executive audiences.

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

jobs.title: Senior Battery Cell Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is hiring a Senior Battery Engineer focused on Cell Engineering to evaluate, qualify, and improve lithium-ion cells for current and future products. You will apply expertise in electrochemistry, cell design, testing, manufacturing, and failure analysis to ensure battery cells meet performance, safety, reliability, and product integration requirements.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Evaluate new cell designs, chemistries, form factors, and suppliers against product specifications and acceptance criteria.

  • Develop and execute cell qualification plans across incoming and outgoing quality control, performance, safety, reliability, environmental, and life-cycle testing.

  • Plan and conduct design of experiments (DOEs) to optimize cells for fit and performance needs.

  • Collaborate with battery system engineers to translate cell attributes into pack designs that meet overall product requirements.

  • Operate battery cyclers, environmental chambers, and laboratory equipment; create representative test profiles and analyze electrochemical data.

  • Partner with suppliers and cross-functional engineering teams to support process qualification, manufacturing readiness, and battery integration.

  • Lead cell-related failure investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective-action verification with suppliers and third-party laboratories.

  • Document and communicate qualification results, technical risks, and recommendations through specifications, reports, and design reviews.

  • Ability to travel up to 15% domestically and internationally to support supplier visits, factory audits, qualification activities, and failure investigations.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field with 5+ years of relevant experience; or a master’s degree or PhD with 2+ years of relevant experience.

  • Strong understanding of lithium-ion electrochemistry, cell design, manufacturing processes, and degradation mechanisms.

  • Hands-on experience with cell characterization, qualification testing, and battery cyclers such as Arbin, Maccor, or similar systems.

  • Experience analyzing battery data, conducting failure investigations, and developing clear technical recommendations.

  • Experience collaborating with battery suppliers, manufacturing partners, and cross-functional product development teams.

  • Experience with Python, MATLAB, Minitab, JMP, or similar tools for data processing, statistical analysis, and visualization.

  • Familiarity with cell teardown, cross-sectioning, microscopy, CT scanning, gas analysis, or other advanced failure analysis techniques.

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

WHOOP is hiring a Senior Battery Engineer focused on Cell Engineering to evaluate, qualify, and improve lithium-ion cells for current and future products. You will apply expertise in electrochemistry, cell design, testing, manufacturing, and failure analysis to ensure battery cells meet performance, safety, reliability, and product integration requirements.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Evaluate new cell designs, chemistries, form factors, and suppliers against product specifications and acceptance criteria.

 - Develop and execute cell qualification plans across incoming and outgoing quality control, performance, safety, reliability, environmental, and life-cycle testing.

 - Plan and conduct design of experiments (DOEs) to optimize cells for fit and performance needs.

 - Collaborate with battery system engineers to translate cell attributes into pack designs that meet overall product requirements.

 - Operate battery cyclers, environmental chambers, and laboratory equipment; create representative test profiles and analyze electrochemical data.

 - Partner with suppliers and cross-functional engineering teams to support process qualification, manufacturing readiness, and battery integration.

 - Lead cell-related failure investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective-action verification with suppliers and third-party laboratories.

 - Document and communicate qualification results, technical risks, and recommendations through specifications, reports, and design reviews.

 - Ability to travel up to 15% domestically and internationally to support supplier visits, factory audits, qualification activities, and failure investigations.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field with 5+ years of relevant experience; or a master’s degree or PhD with 2+ years of relevant experience.

 - Strong understanding of lithium-ion electrochemistry, cell design, manufacturing processes, and degradation mechanisms.

 - Hands-on experience with cell characterization, qualification testing, and battery cyclers such as Arbin, Maccor, or similar systems.

 - Experience analyzing battery data, conducting failure investigations, and developing clear technical recommendations.

 - Experience collaborating with battery suppliers, manufacturing partners, and cross-functional product development teams.

 - Experience with Python, MATLAB, Minitab, JMP, or similar tools for data processing, statistical analysis, and visualization.

 - Familiarity with cell teardown, cross-sectioning, microscopy, CT scanning, gas analysis, or other advanced failure analysis techniques.

 - Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.
   
   

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office. 

 

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

 

WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify https://www.e-verify.gov/ to determine employment eligibility.  It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

 

The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.

 

At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

 

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $140,000 - $195,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training. 

 

In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

jobs.title: Change Management Team Lead, Membership Services
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we’re on a mission to unlock human performance and healthspan. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives. Within Membership Services, we bring that mission to life by transforming every touchpoint into a catalyst for progress, so members feel equipped to rise to the moment, every moment.

WHOOP is seeking a Change Management Team Lead to lead the team responsible for helping Membership Services successfully adopt, embed, and sustain operational change. This role will own and evolve the team’s change management framework, including change intake, impact assessment, sizing, governance, implementation planning, adoption measurement, and reinforcement.

This is a people leadership role with accountability for developing Change Management Specialists, setting priorities, managing team capacity, and ensuring changes are delivered consistently and effectively. You will provide hands-on direction for complex or high-impact initiatives while empowering the team to independently manage changes across the Membership Services roadmap.

You will partner closely with Membership Services leadership, Learning & Training, Quality, Knowledge Management, Support Operations, Launch Readiness, and other cross-functional teams to translate upcoming changes into coordinated, practical plans. Through strong leadership, structured planning, frontline engagement, data, and feedback, you will ensure changes land effectively with internal teams and enable Membership Services to consistently deliver the distinguished service our members expect.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Change Management Specialists, setting clear expectations, providing ongoing feedback, managing performance, and supporting career growth.

  • Operate and continuously improve the Membership Services change management framework, including intake, assessment, sizing, governance, planning standards, adoption measurement, and reinforcement.

  • Manage the team’s priorities and capacity, assigning work based on complexity, risk, business needs, and potential impact on the member experience.

  • Provide direction for change plans, ensuring they clearly define the intended member experience, employee impacts, communications, enablement needs, risks, ownership, and measures of success.

  • Lead or provide hands-on support for complex, high-risk, or highly visible changes, serving as an escalation point when barriers could affect adoption, operational performance, or the member experience.

  • Partner with Learning & Training, Quality, Knowledge Management, Support Operations, and Launch Readiness leaders to align deliverables, resolve dependencies, and prepare teams to support changes from launch.

  • Lead change governance discussions, providing senior stakeholders with clear visibility into upcoming changes, readiness, adoption risks, required decisions, and recommended actions.

  • Ensure member and frontline insights are incorporated into change decisions by using employee feedback, quality trends, process adherence, operational performance, and member contact data.

  • Oversee adoption and post-implementation monitoring, directing targeted communication, enablement, reinforcement, or remediation when gaps or unintended consequences emerge.

  • Ensure change plans account for impacts on AI-enabled support and automation, while promoting the thoughtful and responsible use of AI tools to improve how the team plans, analyzes, communicates, and delivers change.

  • Facilitate post-implementation reviews and use lessons learned to strengthen team practices, improve future change delivery, and reduce friction for members and employees.

Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience in change management, program or project management, enablement, operations, or a related field, including direct people management experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to coach and develop team members, set priorities, manage performance, and build a collaborative, high-accountability team environment.

  • Experience leading change through planning, impact assessment, implementation, adoption, reinforcement, and post-launch evaluation.

  • Strong portfolio and organizational management skills, with the ability to balance multiple initiatives, resources, risks, and timelines.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders, navigate competing priorities, and translate complexity into clear direction.

  • A member-first, data-informed approach to identifying risks, measuring outcomes, and improving both employee and member experiences.

  • Strong judgment and confidence operating in ambiguity, making decisions, escalating appropriately, and bringing structure to evolving initiatives.

  • Fluency with AI-enabled tools and the ability to guide their responsible use while maintaining high standards for accuracy, quality, and human judgment.

  • Demonstrated passion for performance, health and wellness, and the WHOOP mission.


Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

 

WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify to determine employment eligibility

 

The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.

 

At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

 

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $60,000 - $80,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.

 

In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

These ranges may be modified in the future to reflect evolving market conditions and organizational needs. While most offers will typically fall toward the starting point of the range, total compensation will depend on the candidate’s specific qualifications, expertise, and alignment with the role’s requirements.

jobs.title: Change Management Specialist, Membership Services
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we’re on a mission to unlock human performance and healthspan. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives. Within Membership Services, we bring that mission to life by transforming every touchpoint into a catalyst for progress, so members feel equipped to rise to the moment, every moment.

WHOOP is seeking a Change Management Specialist to help Membership Services successfully adopt, embed, and sustain operational change. This role will help shape and operate the team’s change management framework, supporting changes to products, policies, processes, tools, and ways of working. This includes change intake, impact assessment, sizing, governance, implementation planning, adoption measurement, and reinforcement.

You will partner closely with Learning & Training, Quality, Knowledge Management, Support Operations, and Readiness to translate upcoming changes into coordinated, practical plans. You will help ensure Membership Services leaders and representatives understand what is changing, why it matters, how their work will be affected, and what support they need to confidently serve our members.

Through structured planning, frontline engagement, data, and feedback, you will identify adoption risks, coordinate the right support, and help ensure changes are clearly understood, effectively implemented, and sustained over time - enabling Membership Services to consistently deliver the distinguished service our members expect.

Responsibilities

  • Manage the Membership Services change intake, assessment, and sizing process, evaluating the impact on both members and internal teams to determine the appropriate path.

  • Build and execute right-sized change plans that define the intended member experience, impacted audiences, communications, enablement needs, milestones, dependencies, risks, ownership, and success measures.

  • Coordinate with Learning & Training, Quality, Knowledge Management, and Support Operations to ensure representatives have the guidance, skills, processes, and resources needed to provide accurate and consistent member support.

  • Assess the impact of upcoming changes on AI-enabled support and automation, coordinating updates to knowledge, workflows, guardrails, testing, and escalation paths to ensure accurate and consistent member experiences from launch.

  • Manage assigned changes through implementation, adoption, and reinforcement, anticipating potential member friction and ensuring teams are prepared to support the experience from launch.

  • Partner with Launch Readiness Specialists on complex initiatives, leading or supporting the employee impact and adoption workstream while bringing frontline and member insights into readiness decisions.

  • Engage Membership Services leaders and frontline teams to validate impacts, identify adoption barriers, gather feedback, and ensure change plans reflect the realities of the member experience.

  • Track adoption and outcomes using employee feedback, training and knowledge indicators, quality trends, process adherence, operational performance, and member contact data; coordinate targeted action where gaps emerge.

  • Provide clear stakeholder updates, facilitate post-implementation reviews, and apply lessons learned to reduce member friction and continuously improve how change is delivered across Membership Services.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in change management, project coordination, enablement, operations, or a related field.

  • Experience supporting change from planning through implementation, adoption, and reinforcement.

  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and timelines.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex information into clear, practical guidance.

  • A member-first, data-informed approach to identifying risks, measuring outcomes, and improving the experience.

  • Fluency with AI-enabled tools and the judgment to use them responsibly while maintaining high standards for accuracy and quality.

  • Demonstrated passion for performance, health and wellness, and the WHOOP mission.

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

 

The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.

 

At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

 

The Ireland base salary range for this full-time position is €40,000 - 55,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.

 

In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

These ranges may be modified in the future to reflect evolving market conditions and organizational needs. While most offers will typically fall toward the starting point of the range, total compensation will depend on the candidate’s specific qualifications, expertise, and alignment with the role’s requirements.

jobs.title: Senior Radio Frequency Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

As a Senior RF Engineer on the WHOOP Hardware team, you will support the development, integration, validation, and delivery of the wireless systems that power WHOOP's wearable products. Working closely with Electrical, Firmware, Mechanical, Manufacturing, and Product teams, you will independently drive RF development and validation activities from early prototypes through production.

WHOOP products rely on highly integrated wireless systems operating within compact and challenging wearable form factors. You will bring strong hands-on RF test and debugging experience to characterize system performance, identify root causes of wireless issues, develop robust validation methodologies, and ensure designs meet performance, regulatory, and manufacturing requirements.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own RF system characterization, validation, and debugging from early prototypes through production.

  • Define validation plans, test methods, and acceptance criteria for conducted, radiated, and system-level wireless performance.

  • Characterize transmitter, receiver, antenna, coexistence, interference, desense, and OTA performance, including return loss, antenna efficiency, TRP/TIS, and on-body performance as applicable.

  • Develop repeatable test setups, fixtures, scripts, and automated measurement methods to improve validation coverage, efficiency, and data quality.

  • Analyze RF performance data, identify failure modes and root causes, and drive corrective actions with Electrical, Firmware, Mechanical, and Manufacturing teams.

  • Guide RF-critical schematic and PCB design, including matching networks, grounding, shielding, routing, component selection, and antenna integration.

  • Apply RF circuit, electromagnetic, and system analysis using tools such as CST, HFSS, MATLAB, Python, or similar tools.

  • Establish production test methods, limits, and correlation studies while supporting manufacturing troubleshooting and wireless regulatory certification.

  • Advance next-generation RF architectures, antenna technologies, validation methods, and manufacturing techniques while communicating technical risks and recommendations across engineering teams.

  • Travel up to 15%, domestically and internationally.

Qualifications

  • BS or higher in Electrical Engineering or related field.

  • 5+ years of relevant RF or wireless engineering experience.

  • Demonstrated expertise in RF system characterization, validation, debugging, and root-cause analysis.

  • Background in conducted and radiated wireless testing, including transmitter performance, receiver sensitivity, antenna performance, coexistence, and desense.

  • Hands-on proficiency with RF lab equipment, including spectrum analyzers, signal generators, VNAs, oscilloscopes, wireless communication testers, and calibration tools.

  • Familiarity with antenna and OTA measurements, including return loss, efficiency, radiation performance, TRP, and TIS.

  • Strong command of RF and electrical engineering principles, including impedance matching, transmission lines, circuit design, PCB layout, grounding, shielding, and antenna integration.

  • Working knowledge of RF test automation, data analysis, or electromagnetic simulation using tools such as Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, CST, or HFSS.

  • Excellent communication skills, with experience supporting product validation, manufacturing, and wireless regulatory certification.

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

jobs.title: Staff Product Designer, Connected Experiences
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is hiring a Staff Product Designer to define the next generation of connected member experiences. In this highly collaborative, 0-to-1 role, you’ll establish the UX foundations for emerging products and create intuitive, cohesive experiences that help members better understand and act on their health.

You’ll work at the intersection of product experience, software, and systems thinking, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Design Systems, and Research. You’ll define interaction principles and scalable patterns, navigate complex product and technical constraints, and shape how members experience WHOOP across an evolving ecosystem.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead the end-to-end design of new connected member experiences, from early discovery and concept development through production-ready designs.

  • Define interaction principles, navigation models, information architecture, and scalable UX patterns that create intuitive and consistent experiences across the WHOOP ecosystem.

  • Design cohesive member journeys across multiple touchpoints, translating complex product capabilities and information into clear, intuitive interactions that prioritize utility and ease of use.

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Design Systems, and Platform teams to navigate constraints, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and bring high-quality experiences to market.

  • Prototype and test interaction models, workflows, and product concepts to validate assumptions, accelerate decision-making, and continuously refine the member experience.

  • Help shape the long-term UX vision for emerging WHOOP products, championing simplicity and contributing to the continued evolution of WHOOP design principles.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 7+ years of product design experience, with a portfolio demonstrating end-to-end ownership of high-quality consumer product experiences.

  • Exceptional UX and interaction design skills, with demonstrated ability to simplify complex problems and workflows into intuitive, member-centered experiences.

  • Strong systems thinking, including experience developing information architecture, navigation models, reusable interaction patterns, or design frameworks.

  • Experience designing highly crafted mobile experiences and working across multiple touchpoints, platforms, form factors, or interaction paradigms.

  • High proficiency in Figma and prototyping, with the ability to use prototypes to explore ideas, communicate interaction models, and accelerate product decisions.

  • Strong communication and storytelling skills, with demonstrated success partnering with Product, Engineering, Research, and other cross-functional teams to influence product direction and bring complex experiences to market.

  • Passion for health, fitness, and building products that empower people to better understand and improve their daily lives.

  • Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

 

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $175,000-$220,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.

 

In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

jobs.title: Staff Mechanical Engineer (NPI)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
At WHOOP, we’re on a mission to unlock human performance. As a member of the Mechanical Engineering NPI team, you’ll help shape the future of wearable technology by developing innovative, high-performance products that integrate seamlessly into users’ lives.

WHOOP operates with urgency because our mission demands it. We build products for people who push their limits—and we hold ourselves to the same standard. We expect engineers to go deep technically, collaborate relentlessly, and take pride in execution. The pace is fast, expectations are high, and the work is deeply meaningful. This isn’t a role where you follow a blueprint. If you’re energized by complex challenges, cross-functional collaboration, and the opportunity to ship hardware at scale, this role will push you—and reward you.

WHOOP is looking for a Staff Mechanical Engineer to lead critical design, validation, and development execution for next generation biometric wearable products. You are a proactive, highly organized engineer with strong problem-solving skills and a sharp eye for detail. You thrive in a fast-paced, execution-driven setting and can drive creative mechanical design solutions with independence and sound technical judgement. You will mentor junior mechanical engineers and collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders (Electrical Engineering, Embedded Engineering, Manufacturing, Product, and Program Management). You will work closely with our suppliers and contract manufacturers around the world to execute engineering validation builds with a focus on high quality deliverables, sharp engineering risk management, clear technical communication upwards and externally, and commitment to product excellence. WHOOP operates with urgency because our mission demands it. We build products for people who push their limits—and we hold ourselves to the same standard. If you’re energized by complex challenges, cross-functional collaboration, and the opportunity to ship hardware at scale, this role will push you—and reward you.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Complete technical ownership (at system level) of a next generation product from design concept to manufacturing release, ensuring performance, reliability, cost, and schedule targets are met.

  • Lead mechanical design, analysis and development of mechanical components around micro-electronics, exact industrial design specifications, product requirements, and manufacturing constraints.

  • Create parametric multi-body SolidWorks CAD models to bring up design concepts that enable simulation exercises, prototyping, and mass production qualification

  • Generate technical documentation such as 3D files, 2D drawings, bills of material (BOM’s), and Engineering Change Orders (ECO’s) following product development cycle timeline

  • Communicate and collaborate effectively across functional teams and external suppliers to align requirements, drive decisions, and resolve issues quickly

  • Drive organized, end-to-end DFM coordination across multiple vendors and manufacturing methods, aligning requirements, timelines, and technical decisions to deliver scalable, high-yield production.

  • Design testing protocols and validation plans, manage testing processes to ensure comprehensive verification and validation (V&V) of mechanical designs.

  • Perform thorough engineering root cause analyses to identify and resolve issues

  • Mentor younger engineers by example through excellence in engineering best practices

  • Willingness to travel internationally up to 20% of the time

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field

  • 10+ years of experience in the design, documentation and validation of complex mechanical parts for medium to high volume consumer electronics

  • 5+ years SolidWorks (or equivalent) CAD experience with best practices for part design/ feature architecture, surface modeling, advanced assemblies, complex configuration management and integrating DFx feedback efficiently

  • 5+ years working with Tier 1 and 2 contract manufacturers in Asia and North America

  • Extensive experience in mechanical design concepts and the manufacture of products utilizing high volume, automated manufacturing processes as well as manual assembly

  • Played a key role in the launch of 3+ products, thorough understanding of full product development process, experience guiding suppliers, product lifecycle management

  • Well-versed in design, prototyping, and evaluation of advanced injection molded plastic components, die castings, metal injection molding, packaging, and material selection

  • Knowledge of Six Sigma statistical methods and how to apply them effectively to make design decisions. Ability to utilize statistical methods such as RSS tolerance stack up analysis and CPK process capability.

  • Strong organization and communication skills and the ability to work well within teams in a fast-paced environment

  • Ability to effectively communicate technical concepts and proposals to leadership upwards (internally), and externally to suppliers and contract manufacturers.

  • Highly organized and methodical; able to create structure, plans, and risk mitigation for open-ended problems and drive them to closure.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify to determine employment eligibility

The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.

At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $175,000-$215,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.

In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

These ranges may be modified in the future to reflect evolving market conditions and organizational needs. While most offers will typically fall toward the starting point of the range, total compensation will depend on the candidate’s specific qualifications, expertise, and alignment with the role’s requirements.
